record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Find physically interesting infinite-dimensional billiards, especially billiards related to equations of mathematical physics, such as multi-phase fluid billiards with reflection boundary conditions on a diffeomorphism groupoid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A (finite-dimensional) mathematical billiard consists of a Riemannian manifold with boundary together with the geodesic flow that reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting the boundary. An infinite-dimensional billiard is an analogous dynamical system on an infinite-dimensional manifold M (typically a Hilbert or Fréchet manifold, possibly a Lie group such as a diffeomorphism group) equipped with a (weak) Riemannian or symplectic structure and a codimension-one "wall" Σ ⊂ M with a well-defined reflection law along Σ.

A motivating example: let D be a bounded domain in R^d filled with several immiscible incompressible fluids, and let G = Diff_vol(D) be the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of D (the configuration space for incompressible hydrodynamics, in the sense of Arnold). The motion of the multi-phase fluid corresponds to a geodesic on a suitable principal bundle (or groupoid) over the space of partitions of D, with the metric induced by kinetic energy. The interfaces between phases impose reflection-type boundary conditions on this geodesic flow, producing a billiard-like system on the diffeomorphism groupoid.

Problem. Construct and study physically meaningful examples of infinite-dimensional billiards, in particular ones associated with equations of mathematical physics. Specifically:
(a) Give a rigorous definition of the multi-phase fluid billiard on the diffeomorphism groupoid Diff_vol(D), formulating the reflection boundary conditions at the fluid interfaces.
(b) Establish local (and, if possible, global) existence and uniqueness of trajectories of this billiard flow.
(c) Identify other natural infinite-dimensional billiard systems arising from PDEs of mathematical physics (e.g. from the Euler, KdV, Camassa–Holm, or NLS equations) by imposing reflection conditions on appropriate hypersurfaces in their configuration spaces.
(d) Develop qualitative and quantitative theory (integrability, ergodicity, symplectic capacities, Weinstein-type conjectures) for such systems analogous to the finite-dimensional case.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open research direction calling for the construction of infinite-dimensional billiard systems (in particular multi-phase fluid billiards on diffeomorphism groupoids) with no specific theorem to prove. No published resolution was found; the problem appears to remain open as a program rather than a single decidable question.

status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem/research direction.
